result.summary:
Lane MOR is done for every brief item. Research: the reference game was studied at both levels. Every direct page fetch was refused by network policy, so the evidence is search summaries, labelled [SEARCH] with URLs, plus one public modding schema that gives table names only. No game file was read, so nothing is labelled [CODE]. The schema download is recorded with its SHA-256. Three other games are compared as genre patterns. The reference has no army morale number outside battle, only modifiers and faction resources. In battle, each unit's morale is raised by beating enemy units, and units rout, rally and shatter.

Design: docs/m7-plan/morale-proposal.md, a PROPOSAL with a reference annex. After a battle, every participant's army loses the DR29 decrease (lane D's net loss), and the winning side's army gains the DA1 rise floor(400,000 x B / (B + W)), with one clamp. The loser takes no extra defeat penalty (option (a), alternative (b) stated). The stock then moves toward a baseline at per-sim-year rates. The default baseline is the top of the scale, which is exactly lane E's model. Option (b), a baseline of 800, lets a victory lift an army above its steady level, and the lift fades. The winner is the side the battle report names; DA6 and DA7 winners will come from lane AP. READING M (b) stays OPEN.

Prototype: lane D's never-raises rule is replaced for the winner, and every settlement is stored as a new MoraleSettlementRow (93 bytes, populated-table test). The baseline is added to lane E's pulse end, defaulting to lane E's behaviour. The in-battle rule "the fight it won" is one shared function called by both resolvers, with coefficient 0 by default (the exact identity). With the rule off, the tactical outcome digest on lane P's tuning battery equals the digest lane P recorded. At coefficient 200 it changes 64 tactical and 31 auto outcomes, and rule P1 still passes 16 of 20 scenarios, with the same verdicts. No golden moved. 23 of 24 mutants were killed by named semantic tests. The survivor (M24) is judged equivalent in effect.
not_done: The in-battle rule 'the fight it won' is implemented in both resolvers but left at coefficient 0 by default. Switching it on (200 proposed) waits for the next parity re-measurement together with lane AP's AutoResolver change (D-079 Q4, D11). Its effect was measured on the tuning battery only, not on the held-out acceptance battery.
No resolver reports a DA6 (defender) or DA7 (ambusher) winner yet. That is lane AP's job; the tests pass the winner such a report would name.

Option (b), a campaign baseline below the top of the scale plus re-basing lane E's low-morale desertion term, is measured as a mechanism but not calibrated and not the default. It belongs with M7.14 (A-38).

The M7.15 hand-off items are not built: the battle's start morale is not checked against the army's stock; the formations of a multi-formation army are not aggregated; one army's battles at the same instant are settled one by one in scheduling order instead of together.
The proposal's later in-battle mechanisms are design only, each with a prerequisite: rout contagion, rally and shatter, commander presence and loss, flank and rear, fatigue.

Research could not read any web page directly (every fetch host was refused): primagames.com, www.pcinvasion.com, www.gamepressure.com, wiki.totalwar.com, www.iskmogul.com, r2encv2.totalwar.com. totalwar.fandom.com and gamepur.com were not retried. Not verified: the reference's morale states and thresholds, its tooltip factors, its ambush penalty, and whether battle results change any persistent army morale.
open_questions: READING M (b), still OPEN as D-082 left it: does taking part in combat cost morale even without casualties? (a) is applied: the casualty-driven net loss only, so a lossless win raises morale by the DA1 rise alone. (b) would add a participation cost in both resolvers or in the hand-off; it moves the parity battery and the tactical goldens, and a lossless win would then net rise minus cost.

For whoever enables the network: the hosts the session refused are listed in not_done. Allowing them (Network access in the environment settings) would let the research annex be checked against the source pages instead of search summaries.
proposals_for_director: No new Director decision is requested. Everything below is delegated design (D-082 section 5), presented for review only.

Size of the victory rise: floor(400,000 x B / (B + W)) micro units for the winning side's army, so beating an equal force gives half the maximum; no extra defeat penalty for the loser. Alternatives are documented: a constant rise, a rise based on enemy losses, a mirror defeat penalty.

Campaign baseline: keep lane E's top-of-scale baseline until M7.14, then move to 800 (lane E's opening 'steady' value) with an excess decay of 600 per mille per year and a desertion term measured from the baseline. Consequence: well-kept armies would no longer climb to full morale on their own.

Switch 'the fight it won' on at coefficient 200 when the parity battery is next re-measured with lane AP's changes. On the tuning battery it left rule P1 at 16 of 20 scenarios, the same as with it off.

For M7.15: an army's campaign morale is the person-weighted mean of its formations; one army's battles at the same instant should be settled together (sum, then one clamp); a battle's start morale = floor(campaign x MoraleMax / 1,000,000), with nothing added.

LocalWinMorale.cs:57 says a formation breaks when it was in the fight before the instant AND is out of it now (proposal §3.2: "in the fight ... before the instant's casualties and is not after them"). findings.claim: In the TacticalResolver the in-battle rule never counts damage from a land formation's crew-served (domain) weapons. The stated rule credits "each land formation F ... that is still in the fight and dealt damage to G within the last pulse length" (proposal §3.2; BattleSetup.cs:57-58). But the hit table is written only in the legacy land Damage handler (TacticalBattle.cs:917). Lane N's guns deal land damage through DomainHit kind 0 (TacticalBattle.DomainCombat.cs:466-472, credited to DamageDealt at :504), which never records a hit. So artillery that breaks an enemy formation gets no rise, and when guns share a break with infantry only the infantry is credited. This is undocumented: limitation 6 (proposal:334) excludes only vessel and aircraft formations. There is no parity effect, since the AutoResolver routes battles with domain weapons to the TacticalResolver.
